title: Streaming structured output: schema safety, escape & truncation retry playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Edge-case handling for streaming structured JSON payloads returned by the Core API (including tool/function calling responses). Focus is on three frequently observed failure modes: 1) streams that contain unescaped user data causing syntactically invalid JSON at chunk boundaries, 2) mid-stream truncation due to connection interruptions or token limits, and 3) client/SDK retries that re-request a stream and produce duplicate or mis-merged partial outputs. Goal: design a compatibility-first server-side protocol and client playbook that ensures consumers can recover valid structured objects or deterministically resume without silent corruption.
proposed_solution: We propose a three-layer solution: 1) Wire framing: emit a small JSON-encapsulated event envelope per stream chunk (JSONL/event-stream) with stable fields: {event_type, seq, schema_version, payload, checksum, resume_token}. The payload is a base64-encoded UTF-8 chunk when raw bytes are necessary, otherwise a plain string for text-safe chunks. seq and checksum let clients verify continuity and detect mid-chunk corruption. 2) Semantic chunking rules: prefer semantic boundaries where possible (close object/array boundaries). Runtime will attempt to flush only at valid JSON boundaries; when not possible due to latency constraints, use the envelope with payload flagged as "fragment" and an accompanying "resume_token" that represents the model KV cursor + server-side partial output ID. 3) Retry/resume flow: server keeps a 24-hour short-lived cache of stream fragments keyed by resume_token. On retry, client sends last-good-seq and resume_token; server validates checksum and returns next seq or returns a compact patch (RFC 6902-like JSON Patch as NDJSON) describing how to merge partial payloads. Compatibility: for legacy clients expecting plain streaming text, introduce a compatibility header (Accept: application/x-redwood-json-seq or text/event-stream). When compatibility header absent, server defaults to backwards-compatible plain streaming but will append a final reconciliation event which includes either a full valid JSON object or an explicit failure code and resume_token. Escaping: forbid embedding raw control sequences in envelope headers; any user content that could break framing must be base64-encoded at the envelope boundary. Truncation handling: runtime will, upon detecting an abrupt end, emit a final envelope with event_type: "truncated" containing last_valid_offset, partial_shape (stringified shallow schema), and resume_token. Clients should treat truncated streams as retriable with exponential backoff and resume_token. Implementation notes: add a minimal envelope serializer/deserialize in SDKs (JS/Python/Go), a server-side compact fragment store with a TTL and eviction policy, and an API for requesting a merged final object if needed.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits framed envelopes for streaming structured outputs when client requests application/x-redwood-json-seq
SDKs (JS/Python) can deserialize envelopes and perform resume with resume_token to reconstruct identical JSON output to a fresh non-stream request
Truncation event is emitted on abrupt connection close and includes resume_token and last_valid_seq
Legacy clients without compatibility header receive a final reconciliation event that contains either a full JSON object or a resume_token to request recovery
End-to-end tests that simulate mid-chunk corruption, network drop, and duplicate retries must pass and demonstrate deterministic recovery in >=95% of fuzzed cases
qa_plan: Unit tests for envelope serializer/deserializer with intentionally malformed payloads
Integration tests: simulate model stream that emits fragments at random boundaries, verify client reassembly matches canonical single-request response
Fuzz tests: random byte insertions, truncation at offsets, concurrent retry races between two clients using same resume_token
Load test: 1k concurrent streams with resume_token cache pressure to validate eviction policy and 99th percentile resume latency under typical load
Manual QA: validate compatibility mode for existing customers using SDK v1 that expects plain text streaming
rollout_plan: Feature gate behind runtime flag for 2 weeks in staging
SDK patch release (minor) with envelope decode support; publish migration guide
Gradual rollout by client Accept header: enable for 10% of traffic day 1, 50% day 3, 100% day 7
Monitor reconciliation failure metric and resume latency; rollback if >2% delta in customer-visible malformed JSON errors
Post-launch: 30-day support window with on-call eng rotation for resume-token incidents

design_decisions: Use framed JSONL envelopes rather than raw length-prefix to remain readable in logs and easier to debug
Keep default behavior backward-compatible: only clients that opt-in via Accept header get framed envelopes; all others receive final reconciliation event
Store resume fragments server-side with short TTL instead of requiring clients to re-request a full non-stream run to reduce cost and latency
Base64 encode only when payload contains control bytes or unsafe sequences to minimize overhead
Use sequence numbers + checksum (crc32) instead of full per-chunk digital signatures to balance safety and perf
open_questions: How long should resume_token TTL be for enterprise customers with strict audit/replay requirements? (24h vs 7d)
Do we allow resume_tokens to be exported in logs for debugging, or should they be redacted by default?
Should SDKs automatically attempt resume on transient network errors or expose explicit resume API only?
How do we version the envelope schema to support future binary payload shapes without breaking older SDKs?
